title: Choose the visual world
question: Choose how the PDPA masking demo should feel during the presentation.

options.label: Microfilm Redaction Desk
options.lineage: microfilm readers, document proofing, and archival redaction
options.thesis: One continuous evidence strip changes from exposed personal data to safely redacted text.
options.viewport: A horizontal filmstrip dominates the workspace: source frame left, masked frame right, with five rule gates and one transport-style primary action.
options.risk: Can feel archival if typography and interaction do not stay crisp and current.

options.label: ASCII Privacy Console
options.lineage: live ASCII renderers and text-mode visualization
options.thesis: Detection density turns raw log text into a living field of protected characters.
options.case: Strong computer-science identity; weaker Thai readability than the proposed world.
options.viewport: The entire interface is one adaptive character grid with input, output, and rule status inside the same typographic field.
options.risk: Thai glyphs and long logs can become tiring at presentation distance.

options.label: Crisis Command Center
options.thesis: Each detected leak raises a visible condition before the system seals it.
options.case: High presentation impact; weaker trust and calm for routine privacy work.
options.viewport: A central source-to-safe schematic anchors five framed rule readouts and one monumental detection counter.
options.risk: Alarm language may overpower the actual masking task.

options.label: Privacy Instrument Panel
options.thesis: Five trusted instruments monitor each data rule while a sixth confirms total exposure.
options.case: Excellent state scanning; weaker source-versus-output comparison.
options.viewport: Two rows of three rule instruments sit above a wide text comparison strip and a guarded action control.
options.risk: Gauges can become decorative when counts are usually small.

canonCard.label: Polished privacy dashboard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar two-panel masking tool, executed at presentation quality.
canonCard.viewport: Header, rule chips, source editor, masked output, and a clear primary action.
canonCard.risk: Clear and dependable, but less memorable than the authored worlds.
